body:
On `84fbf0a0e`, separate gamma and denominator calculations overflow in `StudentDistribution::operator()`. At x = 0, the saved double-precision results are:

| Degrees of freedom | Before | With the fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| 342 | 0 | 0.398650762904614 |
| 343 | NaN | 0.398651612497840 |
| 1000 | NaN | 0.398842557313888 |

Evaluate the density in log space using the existing `GammaFunction::logValue` and `log1p`. Convert the degrees of freedom to `Real` before adding one, avoiding signed overflow at the default 32-bit integer maximum.

Subtracting large log-gamma values still loses accuracy: a saved comparison with Boost.Math 1.83.0 in long double measured about 1.2e-9 relative error near one million degrees of freedom and 1.5e-6 at n = 2147483647, x = 0.

`testStudentDistributionLargeDegreesOfFreedom` checks mpmath references for controls, the overflow transition, larger parameters, a positive tiny density and the default integer boundary.

On Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3.0, Boost 1.83.0, Release, warnings as errors) this commit builds in C++17 and C++20, `DistributionTests` passes in both, and the full C++17 test suite passes. With the production file from the parent commit, the new test fails (`positive argument required`).

title: Fix `StudentDistribution` overflow at large degrees of freedom
